function: Channel estimation, antenna extrapolation and CSI feedback with one learned CNN denoiser used as plug-and-play prior (p. 2).
system: Single-cell FDD massive MIMO-OFDM; BS with 32-antenna ULA, single-antenna UE, no RIS; 28 GHz, 200 MHz bandwidth (pp. 2, 8).
method: CNN denoiser (8 conv layers, 48 kernels) inside half-quadratic-splitting iterations; trained off-line, described as unsupervised, on noisy/clean CSI; no per-task fine-tuning (pp. 2, 6).
data_channel: DeepMIMO ray-tracing scenario O1_28 at 28 GHz, BS3, user grid 2; 100,000 training, 30,000 validation, 20,000 test CSI samples (p. 8).
test_conditions: Train: noisy CSI, SNR 0-40 dB. Test: held-out samples of same scene; one model reused for pilot patterns A-D (128/256 pilots), antenna selections, five compression ratios (pp. 8-11).
baselines: LS, LMMSE, ChannelNet, ReEsNet for estimation; spline interpolation (RBF), FNN-ADEN, CNN-ADEN for extrapolation; TVAL3, CsiNet+ for feedback (pp. 9-10).
metrics: NMSE for all tasks, cosine similarity (CoS) for feedback, and number of model parameters (pp. 8-12).
complexity: 175.2K parameters for the single shared model, stated as 3.6% of the parameters of the compared methods for all three tasks (Table III, pp. 11-12).
openness: Source code at https://github.com/wc253/PNPMT (footnote 3, p. 8); DeepMIMO dataset used (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 8: "generated by the DeepMIMO channel generation platform [38], which constructs MIMO channel data from accurate ray-tracing data"; scene O1_28 at 28 GHz.
q2_support: p. 9: "a common DL model can be applied for all pilot patterns"; p. 10: "different pilot patterns ... different antenna selection patterns ... different compression ratios and quantization bits". The denoiser is trained once, on denoising only (p. 6), and tested on these unseen configurations without retraining (pp. 9-11). Borderline: the scene and the user grid are the same for training and test (p. 8).
q3_support: p. 9: "LS and LMMSE [26], and two DL-based channel estimation methods, i.e., ChannelNet [10] and ReEsNet [26]"; p. 10: "spline interpolation, i.e., RBF, and DL-based ADEN [11]" and "TVAL3 [48], and CsiNet+ [35]"; all compared on NMSE (Figs. 7, 8, 10, Table II).
q4_support: p. 12: "the DL model in the proposed method requires only 175.2K parameters"; Table III (p. 11) lists the parameters of every compared model. No FLOPs or runtime are reported.
q5_support: p. 8: "The source code of this paper has been publicly uploaded to https://github.com/wc253/PNPMT"; the data are the DeepMIMO ray-tracing channels (p. 8).
notes: Eligible: the learned CNN denoiser is the physical-layer prior of the estimator, extrapolator and feedback decoder (p. 6); BS has 32 antennas, so not a single-antenna link. Area 2: all three tasks are channel reconstruction (p. 2). RIS appears only in related work (p. 1), so ris is 0. The paper calls the denoiser unsupervised (p. 2) although training uses noisy/clean CSI pairs (p. 6). q2 is borderline because the generalization is across task configurations (pilot patterns, antenna selections, compression ratios) of one scene, not across scenarios or sites; the reviewer should confirm. q4 rests on the parameter count only. PDF checked: page 1 holds the title and DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2024.3369702.
